newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen extending gains.

text.p: Polish shares rose in lighter volume after recent losses lured bargain-hunters and analysts said demand for large-cap stocks signalled the market could extend Wednesday's gains later this week.
The main market's WIG index rose 1.7 percent, to 13,515.9, and turnover fell 6.3 percent to 79.3 million zlotys ($27.3 million) on both markets as 56 issues rose, 11 fell and 16 were flat.
They said said the 9.9-percent surge by the bourse's biggest issue, Bank Slaski could be perceived by smaller players as a positive sign of returning institutional interest.
"The Bank Slaski strong rise changed the mood on the bourse so much that one can expect growth now," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska.
Bank Slaski surged in the session's top 13.8-million zloty ($4.8 million) turnover, likely on a single, large buy-order.
From among other large-caps Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH) rose 1.1 percent while trading and industrial firm Elektrim was flat.

Some analysts saw the market breaking out of its month-long sideways drift and finding resistance for WIG at 13,700 or 13,900 later this week or early next week, but said higher turnover was necessary to take the market to 15,000 points.
Analysts said moderate 1.4 percent growth in Poland's broad money in November was a good signal showing monetary expansion was under control.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose seven percent in 23.8-million-zlotys ($8.2 million) live trade and rose 3.3 percent in an 8.5-million-zloty (2.9 million) turnover in regular session.
